items.bold: IRAN ESCALATED — launched cruise missiles, drones, fast boats at US ships in Hormuz. US destroyed 6-7 Iranian boats.
items.text: CNN (live, 17 minutes ago) and CENTCOM confirmed: Admiral Cooper stated Iran launched "multiple cruise missiles, drones and small boats at ships we are protecting. We have defeated each and every one of those threats through the clinical application of defensive munitions." US Apache and Seahawk helicopters sank six small Iranian fast boats. Additional Iranian cruise missiles targeting US Navy destroyers and merchant ships were shot down. Cooper said he "strongly advised" Iranian forces to remain well clear of US military assets. Trump said US shot down "seven small boats." This is the biggest exchange of fire between US and Iranian forces since the April 8 ceasefire — Iran did not just warn, it attacked. The ceasefire framework is now under severe strain.

items.bold: SOUTH KOREAN VESSEL HMM NAMU hit off UAE. IRAN ATTACKED FUJAIRAH — UAE's key Hormuz bypass port.
items.text: Multiple outlets confirmed: South Korean vessel HMM Namu hit by explosion and fire while anchored off the UAE. 24 crew members (6 South Koreans, 18 other nationals), no casualties reported. Seoul confirmed the incident. Trump Truth Social: "Iran has taken some shots at unrelated Nations...including a South Korean Cargo Ship. Perhaps it's time for South Korea to come and join the mission!" Critically: Iran also targeted Fujairah — the UAE's major oil export terminal on the Gulf of Oman side, beyond the Strait of Hormuz. The UAE confirmed three Iranian cruise missiles were "successfully handled" over UAE territorial waters, a fourth landed in the sea. Fujairah is one of the few Middle East oil export routes that does NOT transit Hormuz — if Fujairah is disrupted, there is virtually no Hormuz bypass remaining. Brent spiked on this news.

items.bold: ADMIRAL COOPER REFUSED to confirm if April 8 CEASEFIRE still in effect. Biggest military escalation since ceasefire.
items.text: CNN (live 17 min ago) and LBC confirmed: Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, declined to comment on whether the April 8 ceasefire remains in effect after Iran's attacks on US ships and UAE during Project Freedom. This is the most significant signal from the US military of the entire war — the CENTCOM commander will not confirm the ceasefire is still active. If Cooper declares the ceasefire over: full war powers reactivate, Trump has legal authority for resumed airstrikes. Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chair Caine will brief the Pentagon on Tuesday morning — that briefing will be the clearest signal of whether the US considers the ceasefire broken. CNN: "This is the biggest escalation in violence since the ceasefire was announced four weeks ago."

items.bold: BRENT +$3.06 to $111.23. Fujairah attack: if bypass route disrupted, no alternative. $120+ risk.
items.text: Brent crude jumped $3.06 to $111.23 on the Iran attack news — reversing Monday's Project Freedom easing. The Fujairah attack is particularly significant for oil markets: Fujairah is one of the very few oil export terminals that bypasses Hormuz entirely, using the UAE's East-West pipeline from Abu Dhabi directly to the Gulf of Oman coast. If Iran can disrupt Fujairah, there is virtually no safe alternative for Middle East crude exports. The pre-war Hormuz bypass capacity was ~5-6 Mbpd (Petroline to Yanbu + Abu Dhabi to Fujairah) vs the 20 Mbpd that normally transited Hormuz. If Fujairah is taken offline: Brent risk rises to $120-130 even from current $111.

items.bold: TRUMP: Iran negotiators "far more malleable." BESSENT urged CHINA to pressure Iran. TRUMP-XI to discuss Hormuz next week.
items.text: CNN (live) confirmed: Trump told Fox News on Monday that Iranian negotiators were being "far more malleable" than they were previously — even as Project Freedom was under military attack. LBC confirmed: US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged China to step up its diplomatic efforts with Iran to help international shipping resume through Hormuz. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping plan to discuss the Hormuz situation when they meet next week. China is Iran's largest crude oil buyer (~1.5 Mbpd from Iran) and largest trading partner — Beijing has unique leverage over Tehran that no other country possesses. If China steps up pressure: Iran may be forced to allow more Hormuz commercial traffic. The Trump-Xi Hormuz discussion next week is now the single most important diplomatic event on the horizon.

military.t: IRAN ESCALATED — Cruise Missiles, Drones, Fast Boats at US Ships. US Destroyed 6-7 Iranian Boats.
military.d: CNN (live 17 min ago), CENTCOM, and Spokesman-Review/Reuters confirmed: Admiral Cooper stated Iran launched "multiple cruise missiles, drones and small boats at ships we are protecting. We have defeated each and every one of those threats through the clinical application of defensive munitions." US Apache and Seahawk helicopters sank six Iranian fast boats. Iranian cruise missiles and drones targeting US Navy destroyers and merchant ships were shot down. Trump (Truth Social): "We've shot down seven small Boats or, as they like to call them, 'fast' Boats. It's all they have left." This is the largest direct US-Iran military exchange since the April 8 ceasefire. The ceasefire framework has been severely breached — from both sides operating in Hormuz simultaneously with live fire.

military.t: SOUTH KOREAN VESSEL HMM NAMU Hit. IRAN ATTACKED UAE + FUJAIRAH Oil Port. Biggest Escalation Since April 8.
military.d: CBS News live and Tribune India confirmed: South Korean cargo vessel HMM Namu hit by explosion and fire while anchored off the UAE. 24 crew members (6 South Koreans, 18 others), no casualties. Seoul confirmed. The UAE Ministry of Defence confirmed Iran fired three cruise missiles at UAE territorial waters — all intercepted. A fourth landed in the sea. Iran also targeted Fujairah — the UAE's major oil terminal on the Gulf of Oman side, one of the last remaining Middle East oil bypass routes. CNN: "This is the biggest escalation in violence since the ceasefire was announced four weeks ago." Egypt and the Gulf Cooperation Council condemned Iran's attack on the commercial vessel. Trump invited South Korea to "join the mission."

military.t: ADMIRAL COOPER Refused to Confirm Ceasefire Status. Pentagon Briefing Hegseth + Caine Tuesday.
military.d: CNN (live) and LBC confirmed: Admiral Brad Cooper, head of CENTCOM, declined to comment on whether the April 8 ceasefire remains in effect following Iran's attacks. This is unprecedented — the CENTCOM commander will not confirm the ceasefire is active during an active military exchange. Cooper also said the Project Freedom operation is "far more than escorting — we have a much broader defensive package." Trump said Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chair Caine will brief reporters at the Pentagon on Tuesday morning. That briefing will determine whether the US formally declares the ceasefire over — which would reactivate full war powers and likely trigger resumed airstrikes on Iranian nuclear and military infrastructure. The most consequential military press conference of the war is scheduled for Tuesday morning.

military.t: TRUMP: Iran "Far More Malleable." BESSENT Urged China to Pressure Iran. TRUMP-XI Hormuz Discuss Next Week.
military.d: CNN (live) confirmed: Trump told Fox News that Iranian negotiators were being "far more malleable than previously" — even as Project Freedom was under military attack. LBC confirmed: US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged China to step up diplomatic efforts with Iran to help international shipping resume through Hormuz. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping plan to discuss Hormuz when they meet next week. China is Iran's largest crude oil buyer (~1.5 Mbpd from Iran) and largest trading partner. If China applies economic pressure — threatening to reduce Iranian oil purchases unless Hormuz opens — Tehran faces an existential choice. The Trump-Xi Hormuz discussion next week is now the single most important diplomatic event of the war. Trump also warned Iran would be "blown off the face of the Earth" if it attacks US ships.

military.t: BRENT +$3.06 to $111.23. Fujairah Attack = India Loses Bypass Route. Kharif Emergency Deepens.

The Fujairah attack is critical: Fujairah is one of the few Hormuz bypass routes, hosting UAE's East-West pipeline terminus (Abu Dhabi crude to Gulf of Oman). If Iran can disrupt Fujairah consistently: Brent risk rises to $120-130. For India: Fujairah has been India's emergency crude routing option during the Hormuz crisis. India-flagged tankers have been using Fujairah as an alternative loading point. If Fujairah disrupted: India loses its bypass option. Kharif fertiliser: Gulf fertiliser imports now virtually impossible across all routes — Hormuz closed, Fujairah attacked, mine threat widespread. India must activate emergency alternate sourcing from North Africa, Eastern Europe, Russia immediately.

assessment.headline: DAY 67, 11AM TUE: IRAN ATTACKED US SHIPS IN HORMUZ — cruise missiles, drones, fast boats. US destroyed 6-7 Iranian boats. HMM Namu hit. Iran attacked UAE + Fujairah. CEASEFIRE STATUS UNCERTAIN. Brent $111.23. Pentagon briefing Tuesday = defining moment of the war.
assessment.body:
Tuesday 11 AM IST. Day 67. The ceasefire is under its most severe strain since April 8.

WHAT HAPPENED MONDAY — THE FULL MILITARY SEQUENCE
• Iran launched "multiple cruise missiles, drones and small boats" at US ships during Project Freedom
• US shot down Iranian cruise missiles and drones targeting destroyers and merchant ships
• US Apache and Seahawk helicopters sank 6-7 Iranian fast boats
• South Korean vessel HMM Namu hit by explosion off UAE (24 crew, no casualties)
• Iran fired three cruise missiles at UAE territorial waters — all intercepted
• A fourth Iranian missile landed in the sea near UAE
• Iran targeted Fujairah — UAE's major oil port beyond the strait

THE CEASEFIRE QUESTION
• Admiral Cooper REFUSED to confirm if the April 8 ceasefire is still in effect
• This is unprecedented — the CENTCOM commander will not confirm the ceasefire during active fire
• Hegseth and Caine briefing Pentagon Tuesday morning
• That briefing is the most consequential press conference of the war
• If ceasefire declared over: full war powers reactivate, resumed strikes possible
• If ceasefire continues: escalation contained but framework severely damaged

THE DIPLOMATIC STRAND — STILL ALIVE
• Trump: Iranian negotiators "far more malleable than previously" (Fox News, Monday)
• Bessent: urged China to pressure Iran
• Trump-Xi: to discuss Hormuz at meeting next week
• China is Iran's lifeline — if Beijing steps up: Iran may be forced to cooperate
• Both military (Project Freedom) and diplomatic (China pressure + Trump-Xi) tracks running

THE FUJAIRAH SIGNIFICANCE
• Fujairah = UAE's East-West pipeline terminus on Gulf of Oman side
• One of the very few Hormuz bypass routes for Middle East oil
• India has been using Fujairah as emergency crude loading point
• If Iran disrupts Fujairah consistently: Brent risk $120-130
• For India: losing Fujairah = losing the bypass

INDIA's TUESDAY
• Markets likely gap-DOWN on Iran escalation reversal
• Brent $111.23 — reverses Monday's $109 easing
• Fujairah attack = India loses emergency bypass route
• Pentagon briefing = defining signal for Tuesday direction
• Trump-Xi Hormuz discussion next week = medium-term positive diplomatic hope

VERDICT: The ceasefire announced April 8 is now in name only — both sides are firing weapons at each other in the Strait of Hormuz. The question is not whether the ceasefire has been violated, but whether either side will formally declare it over. Admiral Cooper's refusal to confirm the ceasefire status tells you everything: Washington is keeping its options open. Iran attacked not just US ships but UAE territory and Fujairah — escalating beyond Hormuz. The Pentagon briefing Tuesday morning will tell the world whether the West Asia War has entered its most dangerous phase.
